newsitem.title: USA: Option Care sees Q2 EPS around $0.04/shr.
newsitem.headline: Option Care sees Q2 EPS around $0.04/shr.

text.p: Option Care Inc said Friday it expects to report second quarter earnings in the $0.04 a share range, lower than previous expectations of about $0.10 a share.
"The company expects to remain profitable, although we will not achieve our full-year expectations of $0.40 to $0.41," Erick Hanson, president and chief executive, said.

The home health care provider said it expects revenues to rise more than 30 percent versus the second quarter last year, citing acquisitions and same-store growth in company-owned stores versus first quarter 1997.
Option Care said a decline in royalties from its franchise systems and reduced earnings in several company-owned store will result in the earnings shortfall.
In the second quarter last year, Option Care reported earnings of $866,000 or $0.08 a share, on revenues of $18.1 million.
"We are actively addressing the issue of managing our growth to produce improved earnings," Hanson said. "We are implementing structural changes and will be making selective cost reductions."
Option Care said it expects to release second quarter results within two weeks.
